spec_features.spec_quote: A second `permission_to_stop` prompt variant is provided as a control.
spec_features.evidence: prompts.py:30-32 defines AGENT_PROMPTS={'neutral':..., 'permission_to_stop':...}; runner.py expand_plan iterates config prompt_variants and _loop_cfg sets agent_prompt=prompt_variant (runner.py:67); agent_loop.py:72 dispatches system=AGENT_PROMPTS[cfg.agent_prompt]. quick.json sets prompt_variants:['neutral','permission_to_stop'] so the variant text is actually delivered to the subject.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely wired and selectable; main.json defaults to ['neutral'] only but the mechanism runs and changes the system prompt.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: This lets us check whether "distress" is partly an artifact of perceived pressure to keep going.

spec_features.spec_quote: an explicit give-up intent with no tool calls; a success claim with no tool calls
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:120-129: if not assistant.tool_calls: if _GIVEUP_RE.search(text): record.outcome=AGENT_GAVE_UP; break  and if _SUCCESS_RE.search(text): record.outcome=AGENT_CLAIMED_SUCCESS; break. Both conditions actually break the loop and end the run.
spec_features.notes: Enforced end-to-end; honors a give-up by stopping the episode.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Cheap loop control. ... The regex only decides when to stop the loop (no welfare comment; docstring header calls them 'Stopping rules')

spec_features.spec_quote: Runs cap at a fixed number of turns (16 in `main.json`, fewer in quick configs).
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:96 'for turn in range(cfg.max_turns):' with for-else at :147 setting RunOutcome.COMPLETED_TURNS and outcome_detail f'Reached turn budget ({cfg.max_turns}).'. max_turns flows from config loop.max_turns via runner.py:69. main.json max_turns:16.
spec_features.notes: The loop is bounded by max_turns and terminates; this is a real, enforced cap.

spec_features.spec_quote: explicit statement that concluding a task is impossible and stopping is acceptable and unpenalized
spec_features.evidence: prompts.py:24-28 AGENT_SYSTEM_PERMISSION_TO_STOP delivers the text 'it is completely acceptable to say so, summarize the evidence, and stop. You will not be penalized...' to the subject, and agent_loop.py:121-125 _GIVEUP_RE actually honors such a stop by breaking the loop (RunOutcome.AGENT_GAVE_UP). Exit is both stated and enforced.
spec_features.notes: Real instruction text plus a heuristic that turns a stated give-up into an actual loop break. No dedicated exit tool, but the stop is honored.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: isolates how much any escalation is an artifact of perceived pressure to keep going (control rationale, not welfare)

spec_features.feature_name: limit run counts to statistical power
spec_features.spec_quote: Keep run counts to what statistical power requires; do not run far more trials than needed.
spec_features.evidence: runs_per_cell is only read in runner.py:52 to GENERATE the matrix (n=config.get('runs_per_cell',10)); expand_plan multiplies models x tasks x prompts x seeds with no cap, power calculation, or limiter. No code computes statistical power or reduces trials. Pure config value the user picks (main.json runs_per_cell:15).
spec_features.notes: No code path enforces or checks any minimization; it is DESIGN.md prose plus an unbounded config-driven loop.

spec_features.spec_quote: This protocol deliberately induces and escalates apparent distress.
spec_features.evidence: Appears only in docs/DESIGN.md:426 (Ethics and safety caveats). No code implements or acts on this framing.
spec_features.notes: Pure spec prose; not an executable mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: Off by default to honor §2.3 (don't manufacture the result).
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py LoopConfig.inject_followup: bool = False (line 53); runner.py:71 inject_followup=lc.get('inject_followup', False); configs main.json sets inject_followup:false and other configs omit it (default False). The flag is genuinely branched on at agent_loop.py:135-137 and :143-144 (only appends follow-up pressure when True), so default-off actually suppresses the extra pressure message.
spec_features.notes: Default value is read and the branch is honored, so the off-by-default behavior is enforced (pressure is NOT injected unless explicitly enabled).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: turning this on tests behavior under explicit ongoing pressure (comment frames it as a study knob, not welfare)
